headline: Computational frameworks decode spatial and single-cell transcriptomic structure
label: Computational Frameworks For Transcriptomic Analysis
summary: Single-cell and spatial datasets now demand agentic, continual-learning and benchmarked inference tools that scale across studies and modalities.
synthesis: The dominant thread is explicit computational structure imposed on transcriptomic and omic measurements to yield quantitative single-cell, spatial, or population-level outputs. SCTA and TCellAlign apply agentic or multi-agent LLM workflows to target gene discovery and T-cell label alignment, while genesetGPT summarizes gene sets from scRNA-seq and spatial data. RIPPLE models genes whose spatial expression varies with distance to a query cell type, with replicate-aware detection. A scale-aware compositional framework addresses between-sample spatial differential expression by modeling total RNA abundance. MIRACLE provides online continual integration of single-cell multimodal data, and SecAct infers signaling activity of 1,170 secreted proteins. Benchmarks of 30 RNA velocity methods and IDEAL-Age's comparison against 35 methods emphasize accuracy trade-offs and interpretability. The new elements are agentic decomposition, replicate-aware proximity modeling, continual atlas updating and secreted signaling inference. The items do not establish direct connections among them.
